newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, UAP leads market.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, UAP leads market.

text.p: French shares opened higher on Thursday, lifted by another record close on Wall Street and unchanged interest rates in the United States on Wednesday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 13.17 points or 0.59 percent at 2,230.36 at 0917 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 4.0 points at 2,237.

As expected, UAP soared at the open, rising 17.19 percent on the news that it planned to merge with rival Axa. Axa shares opened 2.21 percent lower. It was the first day both shares requoted since the announcement on Monday.
UAP shares were the most heavily traded on the bourse on Thursday and the stock was also the biggest gainer at the open.
Sligos and Axime were the next biggest gainers.

Sligos was up 14.70 percent after being briefly suspended limit up. Axime was up 4.52 percent at 555 francs. Both shares were requoting for the first time since Axime announced it would bid for Sligos.
Insurer GAN's shares were up 3.42 percent on news the government was suspending indefinitely its plans to sell Gan's profitable CIC banking unit.

Sanofi rose at the open after the company announced on Wednesday that its clopidogrel drug was more effective than aspirin in reducing the risk of stroke, heart attack or death in patients with cardiovascular problems. The drug is being developed with U.S. company Bristol-Myers Squibb.
But Sanofi shares later lost ground and were trading at 464 francs, off 1.28 percent at 0951 GMT.
BNP was down 0.71 percent at 211.20 francs while Paribas was up 2.02 percent at 354 francs. Financial sector stocks evenly split between gainers and losers.
Pechiney slumped 3.38 percent to 214.50 at the open after the company predicted it would post a net loss in the second half.
